executive_summary: EUR/CAD closed at 1.60358 on 2026-10-02, the payload spot date, which is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date. The pair is flat over one month (0.00%), down 1.05% over three months, down 0.80% over six months and down 1.95% over one year. That puts it at the 48th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 1.56817-1.64218, so the cross is mid-range rather than extended. Both dossiers are Bearish on their own currency at conviction 3 (EUR -0.2651, CAD -0.2576 tactically), and both views are built mainly against the dollar. In this cross the dollar cancels. What is left is relative pricing. The Government of Canada two-year carries about 112bp of hike premium over a 2.25% overnight rate, while the Schatz carries about 70bp over a 2.50% deposit rate. That premium is not justified when Canadian core is 1.95% against euro core at 2.4%, Canadian employment fell 41,700 in August, and Governor Macklem's hawkish framing depended on oil near USD 100 while WTI is at USD 91.51. The offset is energy, which pushes the legs in opposite directions: the euro area pays a EUR 28.0bn monthly energy import bill and goes into winter with gas storage near 70%, while Canada sits on the receiving side of the shock even with a USD 14.80 WCS discount. France also adds a sovereign risk premium with no backstop and no Canadian equivalent. The settled direction is Tactical Bullish at conviction 2 (score +0.1827) and Strategic Neutral at conviction 1 (score +0.0792). We would express the tactical view only around the 2026-10-28 BoC MPR and 2026-10-29 ECB sequence, from 1.6000-1.6040, targeting 1.6150-1.6180 with a 1.5925 stop. The main caveat is that the tape is working against the view: there have been lower highs since the 1.62921 June peak, spot is below all three daily moving averages, and 2026-10-01 was a -137 pip session, the largest daily decline in the 130-bar window. Separately, early commentary after the payload has the pair trading lower again despite softer oil.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The policy differential is 25bp in the euro's favour: the ECB deposit rate is 2.50% and the Bank of Canada Overnight Rate Target is 2.25%, per the payload as of 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-28. The tactical edge is not that level. It is what each curve has priced against its own central bank. The German two-year Schatz at 3.20% sits about 70bp above the deposit rate. The Government of Canada two-year at 3.37% sits 112bp above the overnight rate. So the two-year spread is about -17bp against the euro even though the euro has the higher policy rate: the market expects the BoC to out-tighten the ECB. The inputs do not support that. The ECB has hiked twice in 2026 with core HICP at 2.4%. The BoC has held for seven meetings, its trim-median core is 1.95% and August employment fell 41,700. The sequencing makes this testable inside the window. The BoC decides on 2026-10-28 with a Monetary Policy Report, one day before the ECB on 2026-10-29. Both banks are expected to hold. A BoC hold is the bigger disappointment because the Canadian curve prices more near-dated tightening, while the market had already cut the odds of an October ECB hike from about 50% to under 30%. The transmission runs through the front end: Canadian hike premium draining faster than euro premium pushes the pair up.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the question is which central bank actually delivers. The EUR dossier's base case is one more ECB hike, most likely at the 2026-12-17 meeting that carries staff projections. ECB staff have already revised 2027 HICP up to 2.5% and core to 2.6%. The CAD dossier's base case is no more than 25bp of BoC tightening inside six months, against roughly 50bp priced for that window, because the Bank has said it needs to see energy spill into core inflation and has found little evidence of it. The BoC's only other decision in the scheduled file is 2026-12-09, which has no MPR, and no BoC decision appears before 2027-01-29. If both dossiers are right, the policy differential holds at or widens beyond +25bp for the euro, while the two curves price it moving in CAD's favour. That is the strategic edge. Delivery risk exists on both sides. France caps the ECB, with the OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp. A Hormuz re-escalation that took WTI back above USD 100 would restore the hiking precondition Governor Macklem set out. Both caps are credible, so confidence stays modest. Carry is positive but negligible against the estimated vol.

Headline inflation is energy-driven on both sides (HICP 3.2%; Canadian CPI 3.0% with gasoline +22.8%), but core diverges: euro-area core HICP is 2.4% against a BoC trim-median average of 1.95%, which is below target. Higher underlying inflation plus firmer activity surprises justifies relatively more hawkish policy, and that reaches the pair through the rate channel. The weak spot is the euro-area consumer (GfK -30.6; retail sales -0.6% m/m), which caps confidence. The near-dated releases all lean towards a wider gap: euro flash HICP on 2026-10-02 (tracking 3.8%), the Canadian LFS on 2026-10-09 and Canadian CPI on 2026-10-19.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months, each economy absorbs an external shock. The euro area pays an energy import bill into winter, with gas storage near 70% and TTF at EUR 72.90/MWh, which squeezes real incomes. Even so, ECB staff revised 2026-27 GDP up to 0.9% and 1.4%, and German fiscal expansion (2027 spending +5.9%, defence EUR 109.7bn) supports demand. Canada faces live import bans inside a USMCA that is now reviewed annually, a housing market with benchmark prices down 3.0% y/y, and a gasoline base effect. That base effect pulls headline toward the 2.4% ex-gasoline rate and the 1.95% core as WTI drifts toward the Reuters 2026 average of USD 83.90. The inflation differential should therefore widen in the euro's favour. Canadian headline is more gasoline-driven and will decay faster. Euro-area inflation has a larger services component, at 1.43pp of the August print. The growth comparison is two-sided. The euro-area winter energy squeeze is the main threat to this factor and the reason confidence is only 52.

CAD weakens against USD in risk-off but has the weakest equity beta in the commodity bloc, with a USD/CAD to S&P 500 correlation of only -0.2 to -0.3. Current risk signals point both ways. The VIX is 16.07 and up 1.64 points on the month, and US high yield widened 42bp to 302bp while investment grade was static. The S&P/TSX fell 2.85% on the month on losses in banks and miners, which is a Canada-specific risk signal. Meanwhile OAT-Bund at 111.2bp, the widest since 2012, is a euro-specific stress signal. The dominant risk driver is an oil supply shock, not a demand shock. That hurts the euro as an energy importer more than it helps Canada, but the effect belongs to Factor 5, not here. With the domestic risk signals offsetting and low pair beta, this factor is not generating a direction.

That would hurt both legs, with direction set by which leg's domestic stress gauge, OAT-Bund or Canadian banks, leads. The weight is only 0.05 and the honest stance is Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The energy shock moves the two legs in opposite directions. The euro area is paying it: EU energy imports were EUR 41.3bn in July, up 13.9% y/y, for a monthly energy deficit of EUR 28.0bn. German import prices are up 8.3% against export-side PPI of 4.6%, an adverse terms-of-trade wedge, and TTF is EUR 72.90/MWh. Canada is a net beneficiary, though less than headline Brent implies. Energy exports hit a record C$60.6bn and pushed the Q2 current account to a C$8.8bn surplus. However, the Brent-WTI spread is USD 11.05 and WCS trades USD 14.80 under WTI, so the realised Canadian barrel is near USD 76.70. Canada's gas prices off Henry Hub at USD 2.90, so it gains nothing from the European gas premium. Canada's monthly balance is already slipping: the July trade surplus fell to C$0.77bn, and Section 338 import bans took effect on 2026-09-29. Bilaterally, goods flows are modest relative to either economy. Per IMF DOTS for 2024, the euro area exports USD 44.7bn to Canada and imports USD 27.8bn, a USD 16.9bn euro surplus. The 2026-10-06 Canadian trade print is the tactical test for the CAD leg. Netted, the terms-of-trade shock is a euro loss and a smaller Canadian gain, which pushes the pair down.

The euro area pays the energy terms-of-trade bill while Canada gains, even with WCS and Brent-WTI wedges, and France's OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp is an unbackstopped euro risk premium with no Canadian equivalent. Positioning, risk appetite and dollar liquidity cancel in the cross. The edge is that a BoC hold with a lowered oil assumption on 2026-10-28 is the bigger relative disappointment, coming one day before an ECB on 2026-10-29 that is already priced below 30% for a hike. strategic.score_interpretation: +0.0792 falls inside the -0.10 to +0.10 band, so the derived stance is Neutral. The relative-policy case (Factors 1, 2 and 6, +0.2416) is largely cancelled by the euro area's energy terms-of-trade exposure (-0.1218 at the increased 0.21 weight) and French sovereign risk (-0.0406). The score sits closer to Bullish than Bearish, but a winter energy shock or a French government collapse could easily push it negative, and a Hormuz settlement would push it firmly positive.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the pair is a contest between two structural forces of similar size. In the euro's favour is relative central-bank delivery. Both dossiers expect their own bank to under-deliver against its curve, but the Canadian shortfall is larger: the BoC's core is 1.95%, its economy is in excess supply, and its only decision before year-end, 2026-12-09, has no MPR. The ECB's 2026-12-17 projection round has to mark a EUR 51.0/MWh gas assumption to a market near EUR 72.90, which gives cover for the one further hike the EUR dossier expects. Inflation dynamics add to this, because Canada's gasoline-driven headline should decay faster than the euro area's services-heavy inflation. Against the euro is the external balance, upweighted to 0.21. The euro area enters winter with gas storage about 12 points below a year earlier and a monthly energy deficit of EUR 28.0bn. Canada, even with impaired oil capture and live US import bans, is on the receiving end of the energy shock. France adds an unbackstopped sovereign premium into the 2026-11-17 budget vote, while Canada's fiscal drift is gradual and carries AAA-equivalent ratings. The two dossiers' standalone views conflict only through the dollar, which cancels here. The bank consensus (NBC, TD, Desjardins, BMO and CIBC) sees EUR/CAD slightly firmer into Q4 2026 and then drifting lower through 2027 on a Canadian recovery. We are less convinced of that recovery but more worried about euro energy than the banks appear to be. The path of least resistance is two-way within the horizon, with the sign set by the December central-bank pair (2026-12-09 BoC, 2026-12-17 ECB) and by winter gas. Conviction is 1 because the score is a near-balance of two well-evidenced forces, not an absence of evidence. A Hormuz settlement is the one event that would move both forces in the euro's favour at once.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically EUR/CAD offers little in either direction. Among CAD crosses the CAD dossier's strongest strategic expressions are short CAD/NOK and long AUD/CAD, where Brent-linked capture and 225-235bp of carry favour the other leg. EUR/CAD has neither advantage, because the euro shares Canada's exposure to energy and trade shocks from the importing side. Among EUR crosses the EUR dossier's preferred strategic relative value is long EUR/SEK and long EUR/CHF on carry and policy direction. EUR/CAD sits mid-table, better than EUR/NOK, which pairs the euro against a Brent exporter with 200bp of carry, and worse than the euro's crosses against low-yielders.
